title: Keep a biology conversation going
objective: Ask a question, check what you heard and ask one more.

slides.title: Listen for the numbers
body: Practice count in a campus garden
A: How many butterflies did you see?
B: Five on the yellow flowers and two on the white flowers.
A: Did you say five on the yellow flowers?
B: Yes, five.

slides.title: Ask about something you heard
body: Use your partner’s last answer to ask one more question.
What colour were the flowers?
Did you say two or five?
Could you say that again more slowly, please?

slides.title: Share one detail
body: A: Look away. B: Choose a garden count below.
B: Tell A what you saw without reading every word.
Garden 1: three bees on red flowers, one bee on white flowers.
Garden 2: two bees on red flowers, four bees on white flowers.
A: Check one number, then ask about the other flowers.

slides.title: Swap roles and repeat
body: B: Look away. A: Invent a new count for the two flower colours.
Speak for one minute together.
Ask, answer, check one detail, then ask one more question.
Listener: Write down the two counts. Compare them.

slides.title: Show that you listened
body: Introduce your partner’s garden count in one sentence.
My partner saw ___ on ___ and ___ on ___.
Partner: Confirm the numbers or correct one politely.
